techniques.instrument: vernier caliper (+/-0.1 mm; Inoxyd Helios, Hannover) for diameters and distances, protractor (+/-1 deg) for angles, on the embalmed gross specimens oriented on a clear Plexiglas stage with grid lines under a Wild Heerbrugg dissecting microscope (model M5-22991; eyepiece x8, objective x6, reducing lens x0.5); whether soft tissue was removed is not stated
techniques.how: Both pedicles at L1 to L5. Transverse and sagittal diameters: the narrowest pedicle dimension in the transverse and in the sagittal plane (Figs. 1, 2). Transverse angle: angle between the pedicle's central axis and a line parallel to the median vertebral plane, the vertebra viewed from above with its median plane on the stage's vertical grid lines and the superior end-plate in view (Fig. 4). Sagittal angle: vertebra on its side, superior end-plate parallel to a horizontal grid line, far pedicle hidden behind the near one as on an ideal lateral film; angle between the pedicle axis and the superior end-plate line, positive cephalad, negative caudad, caudad ones reported apart (Fig. 5). Posterior-to-anterior distance: shortest distance from the back of the laminar cortex to the front of the vertebral body cortex along the line through the middle of the pedicle used for the transverse angle (Fig. 6).
techniques.magnification: not applicable (direct measurement on the specimen)
techniques.observers: one investigator for every measurement, each data point the mean of three trials (stated once for all diameters, distances and angles, pp. 541-542)

techniques.how: Transverse and sagittal diameters of both pedicles at L1 to L5, the same definitions as directly.
techniques.magnification: technique held constant and calibrated to give no measurable magnification; no correction

techniques.magnification: corrected: a collimator test tool (Radiation Measurements, Middleton, Wisconsin) at the patients' distance and settings read 100 mm as 108 mm, so diameters were multiplied by 0.93 (100/108)

techniques.instrument: vernier caliper (+/-0.1 mm; Inoxyd Helios, Hannover) for diameters and distances, protractor (+/-1 deg) for angles, on routine decubitus lateral radiographs of the lumbosacral spine
techniques.how: Sagittal angle of the pedicle axis against the superior end-plate, both pedicles at L1 to L5; caudad pedicles left out of Table III and given in the text.
techniques.observers: one investigator for every measurement, each data point the mean of three trials (stated once for all diameters, distances and angles, pp. 541-542)

techniques.instrument: vernier caliper (+/-0.1 mm; Inoxyd Helios, Hannover) for diameters and distances, protractor (+/-1 deg) for angles, on retrospective routine CT scans (Siemens Somatom DRH, version G/G1/H), contiguous 4 mm cuts
techniques.how: Cuts parallel to the superior end-plates and through the middle of the pedicles where possible, gantry not always parallel at L5-S1; transverse angle to the median plane and posterior-to-anterior distance along the pedicle axis, both pedicles; L1 usually not on the scans, so no L1 data.
techniques.magnification: distance corrected: a known 100 mm read 55 mm on the scans, so distances were multiplied by 1.82 (100/55); angles not corrected
techniques.observers: one investigator for every measurement, each data point the mean of three trials (stated once for all diameters, distances and angles, pp. 541-542)

within_paper: The 21 Part 2 spines were selected at random from the 49 Part 1 cadavers (p. 543, PDF 3), so Part 2 is a subset of Part 1's subjects: the same measurements made directly in Part 1 were made again on their radiographs, and Table II's direct column is of those 21 spines (p. 545, PDF 5). Inference: the Table II direct values are Part 1 measurements of the subset, which the matching caudad pedicle values on p. 545 support, though the L5 transverse angle (22 deg against 17 and 18 in Table I) leaves open a separate session. The Part 3 patients are different, living people (p. 543, PDF 3) and share no subjects with Parts 1 and 2.
